findings.reason: as written a worker checks the cited followup, finds it resolved and skips the wiring, so the plan would certify a booking that is still off the production path; naming the open owner (or stating the map support-partition call as this section's own clause, with the current legacy read shown as the failing control) changes what the node must land.
findings.text: the added clause "the forward map's support partition calls current.book on topology.read membership (followup f-cfs-wire-current-book), so the solve route books through current.book" cites a followup that is data-status="resolved", and that record's outcome says "Partly landed at merge 7c9d86bd4 … The production support partition (ForwardFluxOperator._support_partition, which calls the legacy fixed-design read) still drives the map and the solve … Routing the solve needs the moment-space formulation, so it moved to f-cfs-moment-space-newton", whose own outcome records supersession and archive/moment-space-newton; the live tree agrees (nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py:3341 _support_partition calls self._fixed_design_read, and nova/equilibrium/forward.py:670 still constructs ForwardFluxOperator for the production solve), so the clause reads as an already-delivered precondition while no open node owns it — a §3 node can therefore pass on booking identity and never touch the solve route

findings.reason: stripping the module and symbol names costs the plan no information (the reuse map belongs to the node brief) and removes a wrong guess about the change radius that a reviewer would otherwise have to test against the code.
findings.text: the section still prescribes implementation: it names the function to write (current.book), the file whose definition it "replaces" (clipped_support_current_moments in clip_quadrature.py) and the call site to change (the support partition in forward_operator.py) instead of stating the quantity booked, its tolerance and its reference, so the plan carries a method rather than the endpoint; the tree already contradicts the prescription in the direction that matters, since nova/equilibrium/current.py:459 defines current.book and its line 498 books through clipped_support_current_moments, so "replaces … in clip_quadrature.py" would delete the integrator the booking currently calls

rubric_items.done_when: pass — s3's done-when carries measurable bounds (budget C·(h/R₀)ᵖ per case, saddle cells budgeted separately, private-flux booking zero, net current at 1e-12 relative, JVP against central differences) and a declared negative control: a level-test membership that is not axis-connected must book nonzero private-flux current, failing by test id with the booked current printed.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — s3 names no gate or log path at all, so nothing it states points at a scratch pad or a node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — current.book, topology.read, clipped_support_current_moments and gs.apply are mechanism names; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag enters them.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the changed clause attributes the production routing to a resolved followup whose recorded outcome says the routing was not done there.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s3 has one deliverable, the booking over the read's membership, and the production-caller clause is that booking landing on the live path rather than a second endpoint.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s3 declares no section-level edge, its deferral names §6's retirement, and the §6-tagged owner of that deletion (f-cfs-legacy-read-migration) is open; the live ruling c-s21-moment-space-superseded explicitly releases the claims that followup was waiting on.
